summary: Cannot confirm whether the mapped source field for 'Settlement Date' still matches 'this definition' after the Q3 platform migration. Two reasons. (1) The glossary holds two Approved entries for 'Settlement Date' (GL-101 v1.0 and GL-204 v2.1) whose wording differs and which are linked as possible_duplicate, so there is no single definition to compare a source field against. Their recorded CDE flags also differ (GL-101 true, GL-204 false). (2) The glossary content available contains no source-field mapping, lineage, or migration information, and checking a field mapping against a definition is a mapping-consistency question that belongs to the Mapping & Lineage Agent, which does not exist yet and has no binding handoff rule. The agent therefore declines to adjudicate and escalates. No candidate definition is drafted because the request does not ask for one and the conflicting definitions need Data Steward resolution first.
conflicts_identified: GL-101 (Settlement Date, v1.0, Approved) defines it as 'The date on which cash and securities are exchanged to complete a trade.' (the actual exchange date). GL-204 (Settlement Date, v2.1, Approved) defines it as 'The contractual date by which payment and delivery of a trade must complete, as agreed at execution.' (the contractually agreed deadline). These can differ in practice, for example when settlement is late or early. The glossary links the two as possible_duplicate. Both are Approved, so neither can be treated as the authoritative one without a Data Steward decision.

Recorded CDE flag conflicts: GL-101 recorded_cde_flag is true, GL-204 recorded_cde_flag is false. This is a recorded flag only; no CDE-criteria policy document has been identified, and this agent does not declare CDE status.
